newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes higher led by SPT Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes higher led by SPT Telecom.

text.p: Czech fixed line telephone monopoly SPT Telecom posted moderately strong gains on Monday helping to push the PX50 index 0.4 percent higher to close at 567.7.
SPT rose 30 crowns to 3,425 in what dealers described as heavy trading after having been somewhat neglected in recent sessions.
"The market had been pushing CEZ and Komercni Banka and SPT was staying behind. It was flat. Today Komercni was not exciting but Telecom was very active," said Ivan Kusacek of ING Barings.
On Monday, SPT announced that it had installed 417,000 new telephone lines in 1996 bringing its penetration per 100 inhabitants to 27.25 from 23.22 at the end of 1995.
It also said it had cut waiting lists for the first time in ten years. However, dealers said techinical factors were more likely to have caused Monday's rise.
Other major issues were mixed. Power utility CEZ rose eight crowns to 1,080 and Ceska Sporitelna gained four crowns to 329.
But Komercni Banka dropped 10 crowns to 2,480 and IPB Bank lost 14 crowns to 321. The afore mentioned five issues taken together account for 54 percent of the PX50's capitalisation.
Overall activity was relatively high with turnover at 1.4 billion crowns.
